component.name: Ettin Edit
component.summary: Fast text and code editor inspired by Notepad++

description.p: Ettin Edit is a modern, cross-platform text and code editor. It opens large files quickly and carries built-in versions of the Notepad++ plugins people install first.

ul.li: Tabs, split view and a customisable tabbed toolbar
Syntax highlighting, folding and completion for many languages
Multiple carets, column editing, macros and powerful search
Compare two files side by side
CsvQuery: run SQL over CSV files
JSON, JavaScript, XML, MIME and HL7 tools
Dark and light themes, and plugins written in Python or JavaScript

screenshot.caption: Ettin Edit with the dark theme
Ettin Edit with the light theme

description.p: Bangla, Hindi, Tamil, Thai and other scripts now show as text instead of boxes.

ul.li: Ettin Edit finds a font on your system for each script its own fonts don't cover: the Indian scripts, Sinhala, Thai, Lao, Khmer, Myanmar, Tibetan, Ethiopic, Armenian and Georgian, as well as Chinese, Japanese and Korean
Letters that join, such as Bangla conjuncts and vowel signs, are drawn joined

description.p: Tables read nested data and HL7: pick the rows out of a JSON or XML tree, read HL7 v2 lab results one row per result, and write nested JSON, YAML, XML or HL7 messages.

ul.li: JSON and XML exports open as tables, with the rows at a path you pick from a list and the parent's fields copied into each row
HL7 v2 messages open as tables, one row per message or per segment, with columns named PID.5.1 and the field's meaning on hover
Explode into Rows gives each item of a list its own row; Flatten Objects turns an object into columns
Export as nested JSON, YAML, XML with attributes, or HL7 v2 messages from a template
Made-up sample files to try it on, in samples/tables

description.p: Tables: open a workbook, a CSV or a JSON export as a table and reshape it step by step for another system.

ul.li: Excel and OpenDocument workbooks open straight into a table tab; any CSV or JSON tab shows as a table with Ctrl+Alt+T
Typed columns, dates read by pattern such as DD/MM/YYYY, and values that don't fit marked in red
Rename, reorder and remove columns, replace and tidy values, filter, sort and remove duplicates, each a step you can switch off or change
Export as CSV, Excel .xlsx, JSON, JSON Lines or Markdown, to a new tab, a file or the clipboard
Save the steps as a recipe and run it from the command line, with --out for a file

description.p: Columns and fields: pull matches out of text, line up columns, pick and sort fields, join lines into a quoted list, escape strings and convert Unix times.

ul.li: Transform > Columns and Fields: Extract Matches, Align Columns, Select Fields, Sort Lines by Field, Split Lines At and Join Lines With, all with a live preview
Escape and unescape strings for JSON, C, SQL, regular expressions, the shell and CSV; Unix times to ISO 8601 dates and back
Sort lines naturally, so file2 comes before file10
Two-key chord shortcuts such as Ctrl+K S, in both keymaps
Preferences, the Recipes window and the Transform dialogs can be resized; the Recipes window can fill the main window
A setting to stop the Markdown preview loading images from the web
Plugin folders added or removed while Ettin Edit runs are picked up, and Define Language can colour numbers after a letter (G-code X10)

description.p: Themes and languages: change a theme's colours by name and define a simple language in a form, without TextMate scopes or JSON.

ul.li: Theme Colours has a Simple view: Comments, Strings, Keywords and seven more named colours that apply to every language
What colours this? shows which colour and rule colour a word, in the preview or the editor
Themes can set the tab strip, panels, status bar and ribbon colours
Every rule of the built-in themes has a name
Language > Define Language: a form with a live preview that writes a .lang.json file

description.p: Opening a file while Ettin Edit is running brings its window to the front again, also when it was minimized.

ul.li: Windows: a minimized window is restored and comes to the front
Linux: the window is activated on X11, and on Wayland with the launcher's activation token
Starting Ettin Edit again with no file also brings the window forward

description.p: Settings in one place: a Preferences window you can search, changes that apply at once, settings files that reload themselves, and an easy move to another computer.

ul.li: Preferences has a search box and new Appearance, Languages and Transform sections
Every settings window applies changes at once and has Undo Changes
Follow the desktop's light or dark mode, and set the interface size
Per-language indentation, and files keep the indentation they already use
Settings, themes, languages, translations and recipes reload when you save them
Settings > Export Settings and Import Settings move everything in one file
A VS Code style keymap in the Shortcut Mapper

description.p: Plugins as transforms: plugins can add transforms that work just like the built-in ones, and Markdown Preview is built in.

ul.li: View > Markdown Preview (Ctrl+Shift+M) works without any plugin or Python
Plugin transforms appear in Transform > Plugin Transforms, the command palette and recipes, with options, a preview and one undo step
Recipes with plugin transforms run from the command line too
Plugins get settings with an Options form, text marks, status bar items and pick-from-a-list
Plugins > New Plugin writes a working plugin and reloads it as you save
Copy Command ID in the command palette and Shortcut Mapper

description.p: Try before you apply: see what a transform will do before it changes your text, and send the result somewhere safe.

ul.li: Keep or Remove Matching Lines marks kept lines green and removed lines red as you type
Filter Through Command, Prefix and Suffix, Number Lines and Reflow show Input and Output panes
Send a result to this tab, a new tab or the clipboard
Suggestions for the file you open, such as Format for one-line JSON
Recipe preview after any step, on the tab or on saved sample text
A Welcome tab, and What's new after each update

description.p: Fixes a flicker on Windows when Ettin Edit starts with the window maximized: the window now appears once, already maximized. Un-maximizing it afterwards gives the first-launch size instead of a window as big as the screen.

Transform first: everything that changes text is in one Transform menu, grouped the same way as the recipe window's Add Step, and Tools keeps the tools that only look at text. There are 11 menus instead of 13 (Theme is under View, Macros under Transform). The right-click menu offers what fits the selection or the file, the toolbar's Home tab puts transforms first with Format, Convert to, Recipes and Case drop-downs, Help moves to a ? button, and a simplified one-row toolbar is one click away. A macro made of transforms can be saved as a recipe, and macros record typing again.

Find it faster: Transform, Convert to has one entry per format and works out what the text is in now, with Read as to choose it yourself. The command palette lists recent commands first, ranks names that start with what you type above the rest, and lists every recipe and plugin command. Recipes keep their shortcuts and toolbar buttons when renamed, and the Recipes window has a Shortcut field, a search box in Add Step and labelled buttons.

Fit and finish: the toolbar shrinks its groups to fit a narrow window instead of scrolling, with a » menu for groups that still don't fit, and the window opens at a size that suits the screen. Screen readers can name every button, including icon-only ones. Theme Colours asks before throwing away unsaved changes. Manage Plugins lists each plugin's commands and shortcuts and has a search box. XML Pretty Print is now called Format XML.

Recipes: save a list of Transform steps (find and replace, line tools, case, conversions, encodings, JSON and XML formatting and shell commands) under a name and run it again on a selection, on every open tab or from the command line. Build recipes with a live before and after preview, or record one by doing the job once. Recipes are JSON files that can be shared.

A new Transform menu for turning text into other text: filter it through any shell command, keep or remove matching lines, count distinct lines, number lines, reflow paragraphs, convert identifiers to camelCase or snake_case, convert between JSON, YAML, TOML, XML, CSV and Markdown tables, and work out hashes, hex and JWT contents.

New AppImage, Flatpak and RPM (Fedora, openSUSE) downloads, each with the licence, website and release notes software centres show. The Flatpak and RPM add Ettin Edit's own repositories, so software updaters keep them up to date, and the Debian repository now carries the app details that software centres read.
Markdown Preview shows images and scrolls along with the text. Hex View can change any byte in any encoding, and binary files, even several gigabytes, open straight into it.
Word wrap keeps up with window resizing on very large files: only lines too long for the new width are wrapped again, the visible ones first, and the line at the top of the view stays put.

Ettin Edit updates itself: Check for Updates downloads the new version, checks it against GitHub's checksum and installs it, then offers a restart. The Help commands are now on the toolbar's Home tab, so they can be reached while the menu bar is hidden.
Find and Replace fixes: \r and \r\n now find line breaks in regular expressions, matches on a line break are highlighted, and \r in a regular-expression replacement inserts a line break.
A tidier window: hide the menu bar (View > Menu Bar or Ctrl+M; tap Alt to show it for a moment) as well as the toolbar, and the app icon is gone from the menu bar.

A hex view that edits a file's bytes, a character panel with every Unicode name, Column Mode, an extended search mode for \n, \t and \xNN, Show All Characters with labels for invisible characters, and a live Markdown Preview sample plugin.
Software centres now show Ettin Edit's licence, release notes and age rating, and the .deb adds the Ettin Edit package repository so your software updater keeps it up to date.
A customisable tabbed toolbar (ribbon) under the menu bar.
German, French and Spanish translations, and a user manual (Help > User Manual).
Syntax-aware code folding, keyword completion and parameter hints.
Preferences, shortcut mapper, theme editor, function list, folder panel, plugin manager, and installers for Windows and Debian.
